title: A refused operation is stored as a denied operation with a deniedReason from a closed set, never dropped and never rewritten
content:
At **admission** a denied write fails the job outright and stores nothing. On **replay** it cannot: a later-arriving but earlier-sorting operation may flip the verdict, so a refused operation from synced history is appended anyway, keeps its index, and carries an outcome:

```ts
type OperationOutcome =
  | { kind: "applied" }
  | { kind: "reducer-error"; message: string }
  | { kind: "denied"; reason: string };
```

`applied` is the default and needs no storage. The other two are the ways an operation occupies an index without contributing state, and they are kept distinguishable: telling a policy denial from a reducer failure by prefix-matching a human-readable message would make a consensus decision depend on a string.

Why not rewrite the action? Substituting `NOOP` collides with the base reducer, where a `NOOP` carrying a skip is the marker that supersedes earlier operations (`garbageCollectV2` counts those markers and ignores skip magnitude, so a denied operation that also carried a reshuffle skip would retract one operation where it meant several). A new `DENIED` action type discards what was attempted, and three consumers need the original: the client matches its own action id to learn which action was refused, sync deduplicates by action id, and re-evaluation must re-append the original if the verdict changes back.

The reasons are a **closed set**, compared as strings during re-evaluation and therefore consensus data carrying no grant id, subject or timestamp:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `no grant permits this operation` | Default deny; nothing applied |
| `denied by grant` | The last applicable grant had `effect: "deny"` |
| `document deleted` | The document was deleted at this position |
| `auth policy version unsupported` | The policy declares a version this build cannot evaluate |

Inspect with `isDenied(operation)` and resolve the effective stream with `garbageCollect(sortOperations(...))` from `@powerhousedao/shared/document-model`. The outcome is persisted and travels by sync, so it rolls out per fleet like the flags that produce it. Sync degrades against older remotes: `GqlRequestChannel` selects the new `deniedReason`/`errorType` fields only while the remote is known to serve them.
